H&P – Detailed

Consult Summary:
31-year-old woman with first-ever 24-hour left-sided throbbing headache and photophobia; telephone assessment most consistent with new-onset migraine, given symptomatic advice and safety-netting.

History:
• Presenting complaint: “Really bad headache” for ~1 day.  
• Onset/progression: Began yesterday on waking; baseline ache with intermittent worsening; intensity described as “quite painful.”  
• Location/quality: Left-sided, throbbing; partially fades but never fully resolves.  
• Exacerbating factors: Light/sunlight.  
• Relieving factors: Lying down in dark; paracetamol gives partial relief.  
• Associated symptoms: Photophobia.  
• Pertinent negatives: No nausea, vomiting, visual change, aura, abnormal smell/taste, fever, coryza, neck stiffness, skin rash, cough, positional or Valsalva worsening, focal weakness/tingling/numbness.  
• Previous headaches: None.  
• Menstrual relation: Last period 1 week ago; no cyclical association noted.  
• Triggers: Possible recent work-related stress.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic illnesses, hospitalisations, or surgeries reported.

Medications:
• Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive) – dose/route/frequency not documented (started ~6 yrs ago).  
• Paracetamol – over-the-counter, dose/route/frequency not documented (for current headache).  
Allergies: Aspirin – causes severe nausea.

Social History:
• Lives with friends/housemates.  
• Alcohol: “Normal amount,” a few drinks at weekends.  
• Tobacco: Never smoker.  
• Recreational drugs: Denies use.  
• Occupation/stress: Work-related stress reported.

Family History:
• Mother: Hypertension and migraine.

Physical Examination:
• Vitals: Not recorded (telephone consult; patient reports no subjective fever).  
• Physical findings: Not recorded.

Investigations:
• None performed. Plan to arrange blood pressure check.  

Assessment & Plan:
Overall Impression:
New-onset left-sided throbbing headache with photophobia, clinically most compatible with migraine without aura; no red-flag features elicited on history.

DDx Integration (brief):
1. Migraine without aura – unilateral throbbing, photophobia, relief in dark, maternal history (supports). Absence of nausea is atypical (opposes).  
2. Tension-type headache – work stress and continuous pain support; unilateral throbbing and photophobia argue against.  
3. Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis – risk factor (COCP) supports; lack of focal deficits or progressive course opposes.

Issue 1 – Acute Headache (probable migraine):
• Assessment: First episode, no alarming features; telephone exam limits objective data.  
Plan:  
  – Start NSAID (e.g., Ibuprofen) with ongoing paracetamol if tolerated; caution re: prior aspirin intolerance.  
  – Maintain good hydration, rest in dark room.  
  – Safety-net: Seek urgent review if headache worsens, changes character, lasts >48 h, develops fever, rash, vomiting, neurological symptoms, visual changes, or photophobia intensifies.  
  – Record/monitor headache frequency; if recurrent, consider formal migraine work-up and prophylaxis discussion.  

Issue 2 – Blood Pressure Monitoring:
• Assessment: On combined OCP; BP last checked ~6 months ago, reportedly normal.  
Plan:  
  – Arrange community or surgery BP check within the next week.  
  – Advise patient to obtain home BP device if feasible.

Issue 3 – Patient Education & Home Monitoring:
• Assessment: Lacks thermometer; unable to confirm absence of fever.  
Plan:  
  – Advise purchase/use of digital thermometer; instruct on recording temperature should symptoms evolve.  

General plan items:
• Follow-up: Telephone or in-person review if symptoms persist beyond 48 h or sooner if red-flag symptoms develop.  
• Documentation: Encourage patient to keep headache diary noting triggers, severity, relation to menstrual cycle.  

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: No objective vitals, neurological or fundoscopic examination possible via telephone.  
● No transcript-DDx conflicts identified.  
● Transcript quality adequate; minor inaudible segments did not affect clinical content.
